title: Micro experiment rotator — personal run ledger
content:
Purpose: quick personal table to rotate small fast experiments across model variants and batching profiles. Keep lightweight so I can triage regressions or cost blips during weekday runs.

How I use it: each workday I spin 6 short runs (rotator slots A-F). Each run is ~50–200 prompt tokens, objective is latency/cost baseline and a small quality sniff. Notes column is informal.

Run CSV (headers: run_id,date,slot,model_variant,batch_size,quant,latency_p50_ms,latency_p95_ms,tokens_out,cost_usd,success,notes)
R001,2025-01-14,A,redwood-small-v1,4,fp16,42,89,120,0.004,yes,baseline after infra patch
R002,2025-01-14,B,redwood-small-q4_0,8,q4_0,38,95,110,0.0026,yes,slightly cheaper but p95 up
R003,2025-01-14,C,redwood-medium-v2,2,fp16,86,170,220,0.011,yes,medium is smooth but more variance
R004,2025-01-15,A,redwood-small-q4_0,16,q4_0,45,102,140,0.0047,yes,bursting increases p95
R005,2025-01-15,B,redwood-small-v1,8,fp16,40,88,130,0.008,yes,consistent with earlier
R006,2025-01-15,C,redwood-medium-q8_0,4,q8_0,92,205,230,0.0065,no,garbled outputs on safety prompts
R007,2025-01-20,A,redwood-small-v1,4,fp16,39,82,115,0.0039,yes,baseline stable after kernel bump
R008,2025-01-20,B,redwood-small-q4_0,8,q4_0,36,90,105,0.0024,yes,good throughput, cost-win for warm cache
R009,2025-01-20,D,redwood-tiny-v1,32,int8,28,64,80,0.0018,yes,cheap but quality drop on long prompts
R010,2025-01-21,E,redwood-small-q4_0,8,q4_0,40,98,120,0.0026,yes,spike in p95 attributed to noisy neighbor
R011,2025-01-22,F,redwood-medium-v2,6,fp16,88,160,215,0.010,yes,good for throughput test
R012,2025-01-29,A,redwood-small-q4_0,8,q4_0,37,92,112,0.0025,yes,repeat of best config

Quick observations:
- q4_0 gives consistent cost reduction (~30–40%) vs fp16 for small workloads but slightly higher p95 in noisy conditions.
- Higher batch sizes (16+) can lower per-token cost but increase p95; for user-interactive targets keep <=8.
- q8_0 on medium-sized models is unpredictable on safety probes — raise a flag before recommending for prod.

Mini rotator schedule (personal):
- Slot A: warm baseline (small-v1, batch 4)
- Slot B: cost probe (small-q4_0, batch 8)
- Slot C: throughput / medium check (medium-v2, batch 2–6)
- Slot D: tiny/ultra-low cost probe (tiny-v1, high batch)
- Slot E: retry slot for anomalies
- Slot F: manual QA / safety probe

Next quick steps (todo):
- Re-run flagged R006 with a smaller prompt set and record exact failing prompts (owner: me).
- Add short automated script to annotate runs with node-region and memory pressure (junior script, link to PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-scripts/pull/54).
- Share summary of rotator results in #applied-ml on Friday with top 3 config recs.

Notes-to-self: keep table below 20 runs per week; archive older runs to Drive folder if cluster changes. Use this sheet as first-line triage before filing infra tickets.

Scratch area (one-liners):
- If p95 > 2x p50 -> investigate background batching and kernel contention.
- Cheap but noisy: mark q4_0 as 'experimental' for safety-critical flows.
- Consider adding a small BLEU/ROUGE sniff for medium runs to detect quality regressions.
